name: Correlation — Single Source Firing Multiple High-Severity Detections
description: A single source IP triggered 2 or more distinct high- or critical-severity detections still open within 24 hours — a meta-correlation that promotes a multi-stage attack chain from one entity into a single incident. Rather than detecting a technique, it fuses existing alerts by source.ip so an analyst sees the campaign, not scattered signals. Because it spans techniques, it should carry the union of contributing techniques rather than a single ATT&CK tag.
note:
### Investigation
1. Read the rules list — are the contributing detections independent stages (recon + credential access + lateral movement) or the same behaviour double-counted?
2. Confirm source.ip is a real adversary foothold and not a busy mgmt/security scanner that legitimately trips behavioural rules.
3. Rebuild the timeline from first_seen across the contributing alerts to establish sequence and dwell.
4. Pivot into each contributing alert for the actor accounts, target hosts, and techniques involved.
5. Escalate to incident when 2+ genuinely independent tactics converge on one non-infrastructure source.

### False positives / benign
A busy management or security source (vuln scanner, EDR, monitoring) can legitimately trip two behavioural rules and inflate distinct_rules. More importantly, two of NBI's own rules firing on the SAME behaviour (e.g., idx5 NTLM fan-out and idx10 on one host) count as two distinct_rules without being two independent stages. Distinguish by whether the contributing rules represent different tactics, and resolve the source against known_infrastructure — do not simply exclude scanner IPs, which would suppress a real chain staged from a compromised admin host.
author: raadabujaish
false_positives: A busy management/security source that legitimately trips two high-severity behavioral rules — validate the source and its rules; genuine multi-stage chains are rare.
query:
FROM .internal.alerts-security.alerts-*
| WHERE source.ip IS NOT NULL AND kibana.alert.rule.name IS NOT NULL AND kibana.alert.severity IN ("high","critical") AND kibana.alert.workflow_status != "closed"
| STATS distinct_rules = COUNT_DISTINCT(kibana.alert.rule.name), total_alerts = COUNT(*), rules = VALUES(kibana.alert.rule.name), tactics = VALUES(kibana.alert.rule.name), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY source.ip
| WHERE distinct_rules >= 2
| SORT distinct_rules DESC
